# Vector control for dengue transmission

Dengue transmission in an urban setting is driven by the density of Aedes
aegypti breeding sites within a few hundred metres of the household. Control
programmes that spray adults miss the larvae in the same containers a week later,
so the intervention has to target the aquatic stages.

## Larvicides and ovitraps

Larvicides applied to water tanks and discarded tyres break the cycle where it
restarts; ovitraps measure whether the intervention worked, because the egg count
on the paddle falls before the case count does. Insecticide resistance in Aedes
aegypti is now widespread, so the programme rotates chemical class every season
and monitors mortality in sentinel cages.

Community cleanup of containers outperforms spraying whenever it is sustained:
the mosquito breeds in what the household stores, not in the drain the crew can
reach.
